text: Spelling Quiz Robert finally arrived at Kennedy International Airport in New York. He had decided to spend a week there. He wanted to make this his best vacation ever. The officer who was in the immigration area instructed him to take his documents to the counter down the hall When he arrived there, he saw a bored-looking inspector. “Good morning, inspector,” He said “Are you working early today? It’s so cold.” He noticed that the inspector wasn’t paying attention, so he spoke a little louder. “Here’s my I-94 form, ready for your inspection.” Finally, the inspector turned and said, “Yeah, yeah. Good morning. Just lay it down here and step into the next room." Robert was surprised because he had never imagined someone would answer that way He thought about it and figured that probably it was the correct way to answer in the United States “When in Rome, do as the Romans do,” he said to himself The inspector in the next room greeted him with a smile, “Good morning, Sir. Welcome to America. Is everything okay?” Robert decided to put what he had learned to good use. “Yeah, yeah. Good morning,” he said copying the other inspector’s expression The inspector got really angry and shouted, “I don’t like that tone of voice, Sir! Do you often speak that way? Show some respect!” The only thing poor Robert could say in his confusion was, “But... I don’t understand!” He left the immigration area embarrassed. He forgot the incident, though, as soon as he saw his cousin Sebastian Delacruz. They ran towards each other and hugged happily

text: Spelling Quiz Pam and Linda stayed in San Francisco for a few more days. They visited Fisherman’s Wharf, Alcatraz, and many other places. They had a great time with Sam and Jeff and were sad when the time came for them to leave Sam and Jeff picked up Pam and Linda at their hotel and took them to the airport. “Are you ready to go back to Milwaukee, girls?” Sam asked “Not really, we'll miss you so much, guys,” Pam answered Before they left for the airport, they decided to say their farewells “Well, girls, I guess the time has come,” Sam said “Yeah, it’s hard to believe that we’re actually leaving,” Pam said Linda couldn't control her emotions any longer and began to cry “It’s okay, Linda,” Jeff said. “Please, don’t cry.” “I’m going to miss you so much, Jeff!” Linda said “I’m going to miss you, too,” Jeff said. “You're unforgettable.” Sam interrupted before things would get out of control. “We'd better get to the airport now, before it gets too late. Your airplane departs at 4:00 P.M.,” he said “Hey, guys, before you go, I would like to take a group picture with my camera,” Jeff said Jeff arranged everyone on the balcony of the hotel room, set the timer on his camera, and rushed to join them. “Okay, everyone,” he said, “say ‘cheese’ on three.” At the airport, they said their final goodbyes. It was a very emotional scene. People were staring at them, but Sam and Jeff finally managed to control themselves “We'll see you soon again, girls,” Jeff said. “This isn’t good-bye.” The girls waved goodbye, grabbed their bags, walked through the security check, and disappeared onto the concourse. While they were boarding the plane, they kept thinking they would meet the boys again in the future
